bull.b: Strong revenue and ARR growth demonstrates continued customer adoption of Zscaler’s subscription platform. Recurring contracts, expanding enterprise demand, and broad geographic growth provide a durable base for revenue compounding over the next several quarters.

Robust operating and free cash flow indicates strong conversion of subscription revenue into internally generated funding, even while GAAP losses persist. High gross margins also create meaningful potential for operating leverage as the platform scales.

Rapid growth in Zero Trust Everywhere customers supports Zscaler’s position as a broader security platform rather than a single-product vendor. Wider deployment across users, workloads, branches, and clouds can support durable upselling and customer retention.

bear.b: Ongoing GAAP losses mean the business has not yet converted its strong gross margins and cash generation into bottom-line profitability. This remains a fundamental execution issue and could limit financial resilience if growth or operating leverage weakens.

The expected deceleration from 25% growth to the mid-to-high teens raises the bar for continued execution and customer expansion. Slower growth could reduce operating leverage, make investment payback less certain, and temper the pace of platform scaling.

Higher spending on memory, storage, processors, data centers, and Zero Trust Branch infrastructure can pressure free-cash-flow conversion while demand is being scaled. Sustained investment also increases the execution burden behind the company’s growth and AI initiatives.
